title: My room, your room, his or her room

sections.content: You know *-m* (“my”), *-d* (“your”) and *-a/-ja* (“his, her”) from earlier. They work on home words too, and the noun keeps *a* or *az* in front: *a szobám*, *az ágyam*. After a vowel the ending is short and a final *a* or *e* grows long: *szoba* becomes *szobám*; *tévé* already ends in a long vowel: *tévém*. After a consonant a linking vowel appears: *ágy* becomes *ágyam*, *lakás* becomes *lakásom*, *szekrény* becomes *szekrényem*.

items.spanish: Anna itt van. A szobája kicsi.
items.english: Anna is here. Her room is small.

items.spanish: Az ágyam az ablak mellett van.
items.english: My bed is next to the window.

sections.content: English changes a word in front of the noun (“my room”). Hungarian changes the end of the noun: *a szoba* is “the room” and *a szobám* is “my room”. There is no separate word for “his” or “her”: *a szobája* is either, and the situation tells you.
